sentence: This project combines data from studies of addiction susceptibility and uses genetics tools to find genes and pathways behind addiction-related behaviors.
This project tests whether engineered natural killer cells made from cord blood are safe and work as a treatment for patients with high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes.
This project studies how Toxoplasma parasites use nutrient signals from their host to switch into a latent form.
This project tests whether radiation aimed at tumors, combined with immunotherapy, improves treatment of head and neck cancer in animal models and clinical trial data.
This project helps plan studies and clinical trials, manage data and check its quality, and interpret results for ovarian cancer research.
This project studies how heart cells coordinate the expression of several ion channel genes by forming groups of mRNA.
This project tests a program that uses nutrition support, community health workers and a digital health platform to lower diabetes and hypertension risk.
This project studies how a splicing factor is regulated and which RNA targets it acts on during mammalian craniofacial development.
This project builds fast MRI methods that use deep learning to measure several body properties at once, including whole-heart imaging.
This project studies the cells and molecules behind why surgically created arteriovenous fistulas fail in patients with chronic kidney disease.
This project builds a core that gathers health research datasets ready for AI and gives biomedical researchers help using AI methods.
This project tests how well vaccines built from lipidated proteins trigger immunity and protect mice against colonization, ear infection and lung infection.
This project tries to find out which types of immune cells make the virus in HIV reservoirs, by capturing the virus and sequencing it.
This project tests a combined treatment for melanoma in mice and dogs, using focused ultrasound and a microparticle to activate an immune pathway.
This project studies developmental and stem cell biology and how it could be used in regenerative medicine.
This project studies how Staphylococcus aureus gets the nutrient lysine during infection by finding the genes it needs for taking up lysine.
This project works to understand cancer risk factors, improve cancer detection, and test ways to reduce the cancer burden in the population.
This project builds and tests proteomics risk prediction models that sort people by their risk of cancers linked to smoking.
This project tries to find out whether deep learning on CT scans and DNA methylation can detect early bone density changes linked to osteoporosis.
This project builds an imaging method using engineered T cells to show disease markers in glioblastoma and to track whether therapeutic T cells are active.
